title: Funeral home crematorium and Becker Street housing referred
subtitle: Also: Delaware Avenue sidewalks, 2023 business plan projects, accessibility committee appointments, and six new units at 525 New Dundee Road.
overview: The main item was a proposal to let a funeral home at 507 Frederick Street add a crematorium and expand its building and parking. The application also covers three nearby Becker Street properties with nine rental units. The committee referred the matter to the January 30, 2023 Council meeting {{vote:m5}}. That gives staff time to look at lower parking rates, a possible building redesign, removing Becker Street from the rezoning, and parking options on Becker Street and nearby land.

Residents of the Becker Street homes and other delegates opposed the proposal, mainly over the loss of affordable housing. Others objected to a crematorium in a residential area. Staff said peer-reviewed studies satisfied them on health and safety.

The committee also recommended sidewalks on the north side of Delaware Avenue, the 2023 Business Plan project list (subject to budget approval), and new appointments to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee {{vote:m1}} {{vote:m2}} {{vote:m3}}. It recommended zoning changes for six more units at 525 New Dundee Road {{vote:m4}}. Council will make the final decisions.

decisions.item: Funeral home crematorium and Becker Street rezoning, 507 Frederick Street
decisions.detail: The committee referred the staff recommendation to the January 30, 2023 Council meeting so staff can explore parking rates, building redesign, removing Becker Street from the rezoning, and parking options.
The committee recommended approving the zoning amendment to allow six more residential units in underused ground-floor storage space of an existing building.
The committee recommended installing sidewalks on the north side of Delaware Avenue as part of 2023 roadway reconstruction.
The committee recommended approving the 2023 Business Plan Project List in Appendix B of the report, subject to 2023 budget approval.

The committee recommended appointing the listed applicants and an agency representative to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee for a term ending December 31, 2026, pending ratification by partner municipalities.

debate: Delegates who live on Becker Street and others said the plan would remove affordable homes for parking. They said relocation would cost far more in rent, and that the overflow lots are used only occasionally. Some asked the committee to remove the Becker Street properties from the application or to reduce the parking rates.

The applicant's representatives said the funeral home already has parking problems during peak services and that the zoning rules require the parking. The owner said relocating or building a second storey was not feasible. The owner said the building structure cannot support a second storey, and said the cremator would reduce transport trips and keep services in one place. The owner was open to discussing a smaller parking supply and the purchase of part of Becker Street.

Several delegates said a crematorium does not belong in a residential area. They raised concerns about emissions, smell, wind direction and cultural sensitivities. One delegate said the environmental claims were exaggerated. A councillor asked about natural gas emissions, and consultants said modelling showed the ministry limits were met.

Staff said independent peer review satisfied them on health and safety. They said no complaints had been recorded for comparable crematoriums. They said the proposed parking exceeds the city's maximum rate for the existing floor area. Staff were also talking with the Ministry of Transportation about moving services out of Becker Street and about perpendicular parking.
Councillors asked staff to look at selling part of Becker Street, a land swap, and removing 40, 44 and 48 Becker Street from the rezoning. Staff said they would report back before January 30.
